chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man gave another man money as a loan; upon whom is its zakat, on the lender or on the borrower? He said: 'No, rather its zakat is upon the borrower if it remains with him for a full year.'

I said: So there is no zakat for the lender? He said: 'No, the money is not purified from two sources in one year, and there is no zakat upon the one who gave it because there is nothing in his hand, for the money is in the hand of the other; so whoever has the money in his hand, he purifies it.'
I said: Does he purify the money of another from his own money? He said: 'Indeed, it is his money as long as it is in his hand, and that money is not for anyone else.'

Then he said: 'O Zurarah, do you see the depreciation of that money and its profit; for whom is it and upon whom is it?' I said: 'For the borrower.' He said: 'So the benefit is his and the loss is upon him, and he may wear from it, marry from it, and eat from it, and it is not fitting for him not to purify it, but rather he should purify it, for it is upon him.'

key_terms.حَوْلٌ: A full lunar year of holding

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying zakat on money that has been lent as a loan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that zakat on a loan (*qardh*) is the borrower's responsibility, as the funds are in their possession and they enjoy the usufruct and bear the risk. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that zakat follows the actual holder of the wealth during the lunar year, rather than the original owner who has temporarily parted with it. The Imam further notes that the borrower cannot avoid zakat by claiming the money is not theirs, as it is effectively their property while in their hands.
